summary: Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Glasgow, SOAS, Oxford, and Yale. His career included professorships at the University of Birmingham, Lancaster University (1967–1982), and UC Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University in 2015 under Peter Bisschop, also studying under Diwakar Acharya, Bhim Kandel, and Kashinath Nyaupane. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Leiden University.

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti (1893–1956) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Cambridge (Ph.D.), Paris, and Berlin. He taught at Calcutta and later served at the Archaeological Survey of India, becoming its Director General from 1948 to 1950.

Nirbhay N. Singh works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He served as Director of the Commonwealth Institute for Family Studies, Professor at Virginia Commonwealth University, and Clinical Professor of Psychiatry and Health Behavior at Augusta University.

Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a historian and Tibetologist who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He worked at the National Archives of India and served as the founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987).
Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College around 2015, studying under MA supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.
Noa Gal is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy degree at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (Wolfson College) in 2003 under Richard Gombrich, having also studied under Shlomo Biderman. She has been a Visiting Research Fellow at Stanford University.

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist who earned his degrees, including a doctorate, at the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and Taisho University.
Noboru Ueda works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He held positions at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and Mejiro University, where he was attested as a professor in 2015.

Nobuchiyo Kotani (born 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, Hajime Sakurabe, and others, later serving as professor at Otani University and president of its junior college.

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara. He held assistant professor posts at the University of Toronto (attested 1969) and Kyoto University (attested 1979).

Nobuhiro Ota (born 1969) is an Indologist and historian who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. After research fellowships there, he joined Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, advancing from assistant in 2002 to professor in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University and served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi (born 1932) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Rissho University from 1955 to 1959 and was attested as an assistant professor there in 1972.

Nobumasa Miyazaki (born 1978) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctorate at the University of Tokyo in 2009. He held posts at Toyo University, Tokyo University of Agriculture, and the University of Tokyo.

Nobumi Iyanaga (born 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held positions at the University of Tokyo and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient's Tokyo Centre (2008–2014).

Nobumichi Kusumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.
Nobuo Otsuka (born 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a researcher in 1995.

Nobuyoshi Yamabe (born 1960) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Osaka University, Otani University, and Yale University (Ph.D. 1999). He held posts at several junior colleges, Tokyo University of Agriculture, and Waseda University (professor 2015).
